# Emergency fund and monthly budget

Our household money rules, from the Saturday we sat down with the spreadsheet.

## How big an emergency fund

The target is three to six months of essential expenses: rent or mortgage, food, utilities, insurance, minimum debt payments and transportation. Start with a first goal of $1,000, because most surprises are car and appliance repairs.

## Where to keep the fund

Keep it in a high-yield savings account at an insured bank: separate from checking, easy to reach in a day or two, and not invested in stocks.

## Debt or savings first

Do not skip the starter fund to pay off debt, or the next flat tire goes on the credit card. Order: build $1,000 first, then put every extra dollar toward debt with a high interest rate (roughly anything above 8%), and then grow the emergency fund to three months of expenses. Cheap debt, such as a low-rate mortgage, can wait.

## The 50/30/20 split

A rough starting point: 50% of take-home pay for needs, 30% for wants and 20% for saving and extra debt payments. In an expensive city, needs may run 60%, and wants shrink to fit.

## Sinking funds

Set aside a little each month for bills that come once a year: insurance premiums, car registration, gifts and vacations. It turns a $1,200 surprise into a $100 monthly habit.

## Irregular income

When pay varies, budget from the lowest month in the last year, and put anything above it into the emergency fund and the next month's buffer.
